sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Roderick Edwin Liddle (1 April 1960 – 2 August 2026) was a British journalist and broadcaster.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He was an editor of BBC Radio 4's Today and an associate editor of The Spectator.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Liddle began his career at the South Wales Echo, then worked for the Labour Party, and later joined the BBC.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He became editor of the Today programme in 1998, resigning in 2002 after his employers objected to one of his articles in The Guardian.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Up until his death, he wrote for The Sunday Times, The Spectator and The Sun, among other publications.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: His journalism was often the subject of criticism and controversy.

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: Liddle wrote the short story collection Too Beautiful for You (2003) and the novel Love Will Destroy Everything (2007), along with The Best of Liddle Britain (2007) and the semi-autobiographical Selfish, Whining Monkeys (2014).

sentences.section: (lead)
sentences.text: He also presented television programmes, including The New Fundamentalists, The Trouble with Atheism, and Immigration Is A Time Bomb.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Roderick Edwin Liddle was born on 1 April 1960 in Sidcup, Kent.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Aged eight he moved to Nunthorpe, Middlesbrough, and was educated at Laurence Jackson School and Prior Pursglove Sixth Form College, both in the nearby town of Guisborough.

sentences.section: Early life
sentences.text: Liddle attended the London School of Economics (LSE) as a mature student, reading social psychology.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: Liddle's early career in journalism was with the South Wales Echo in Cardiff, where he was a general news reporter and, for a time, the rock and pop writer.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: He returned to journalism after graduating from the LSE, and was taken on as a trainee producer by the BBC.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: Liddle was appointed editor of the BBC Radio 4 programme Today in 1998.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: The programme had a reputation for its political interviews, but Liddle tried, with some success, to improve the show's investigative journalism.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: To this end, he hired journalists from outside the BBC.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: Among these was Andrew Gilligan, who joined from The Sunday Telegraph in 1999.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: Gilligan's 29 May 2003 report on Todaythat the British government had "sexed up" the intelligence dossier on Iraq, a report broadcast after Liddle had left the programmebegan a chain of events that included the death in July that year of David Kelly, the weapons inspector who was Gilligan's source, and the subsequent Hutton Inquiry, a public inquiry into the circumstances of Kelly's death.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: Liddle defended Gilligan throughout the controversy.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: Under Liddle's editorship, Today won several awards: a Sony Silver in 2002 for reports by Barnie Choudhury and Mike Thomson into the causes of race riots in the north of England; a Sony Bronze in 2003 for an investigation by Angus Stickler into paedophile priests; and an Amnesty International Media Award in 2003 for Gilligan's investigation into the sale of illegal landmines, an investigation that attracted a lengthy legal action.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: While working for Today, Liddle also wrote a column for The Guardian.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: On 25 September 2002, referring in it to a march organised by the Countryside Alliance in defence of fox hunting, Liddle wrote that readers may have forgotten why they voted Labour in 1997, but would remember once they saw the people campaigning to save hunting.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: His column led The Daily Telegraph to accuse Liddle of bias and of endangering democracy.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: The BBC concluded that Liddle's comments breached his commitment to impartiality as a BBC programme editor, and gave him an ultimatum to stop writing his column or resign from his position on Today.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: He resigned on 30 September 2002.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: He said later that, when he was editor, he was ordered by BBC management to sack Frederick Forsyth from the programme, and speculated that it was because of Forsyth's right-wing political views.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: The BBC replied that the decision was made for editorial reasons.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: Following his departure from Today, Liddle began writing regularly for The Spectator in October 2002.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: He continued to write regularly for The Spectator until his death.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: He continued to write for The Guardian and became an associate editor with The Spectator.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: He also wrote for the men's magazines GQ and Arena, and had a weekly column for The Sunday Times.

sentences.section: Radio and print journalism
sentences.text: Beginning in January 2025, he presented a Saturday morning show on Times Radio.

sentences.section: Controversial writings
sentences.text: Liddle's columns were often seen as controversial.

sentences.section: Controversial writings
sentences.text: The Press Complaints Commission (PCC) censured his blog in 2010, making him the first journalist to have a blog censured in the UK.

sentences.section: Controversial writings
sentences.text: While critics accused him of being racist and misogynist, he defended his work as provoking debate or being satirical.

sentences.section: Comments on Harriet Harman
sentences.text: In August 2009, in his Spectator blog he wrote about Harriet Harman, deputy leader of the Labour Party, in unflattering terms.

sentences.section: Comments on Harriet Harman
sentences.text: Liddle began the article by asking: "SoHarriet Harman, then.

sentences.section: Comments on Harriet Harman
sentences.text: Would you?

sentences.section: Comments on Harriet Harman
sentences.text: I mean after a few beers obviously, not while you were sober."

sentences.section: Comments on Harriet Harman
sentences.text: Tanya Gold wrote in The Guardian that it was a "tissue-thin polemic" and pointing out that it was The Spectators cover story that week.

sentences.section: Comments on Harriet Harman
sentences.text: In The Observer nearly two months later, Rachel Cooke recalled finding Liddle's piece "disgusting".

sentences.section: Comments on Harriet Harman
sentences.text: Cooke went on to say: "I would still like to do something really unpleasant to the man who wrote [the article]."

sentences.section: Comments on Harriet Harman
sentences.text: Liddle said two months later that the Harman column "was supposed to be a parody of guttural, base sexism", a joke he assumed readers would understand.

sentences.section: Comments on Harriet Harman
sentences.text: After the negative response from Gold (and then Cooke, among other female journalists) he continued: "And then I suppose I came to the conclusion – gradually – that I must have got it wrong."

sentences.section: Comments on Harriet Harman
sentences.text: In June 2014, he said that of those he had offended, Harman was the one person to whom he would apologise.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: In November 2009, again for The Spectator website, Liddle offered "a quick update on what the Muslim savages are up to", a brief article about the stoning to death of a 20-year-old woman in Somalia after she was accused of adultery, and the similar death of a 13-year-old the year before.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: He made remarks, considered sarcastic, that read: "Incidentally, many Somalis have come to Britain as immigrants recently, where they are widely admired for their strong work ethic, respect for the law and keen, piercing, intelligence."

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: In December 2009, on his Spectator blog, Liddle referred to two black music producers, Brandon Jolie and Kingsley Ogundele, who had plotted to kill Jolie's 15-year-old pregnant girlfriend, as "human filth" and said the incident was not an anomaly.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: He continued:

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: The overwhelming majority of street crime, knife crime, gun crime, robbery and crimes of sexual violence in London is carried out by young men from the African-Caribbean community.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: Of course, in return, we have rap music, goat curry and a far more vibrant and diverse understanding of cultures which were once alien to us.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: For which, many thanks.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: When he was accused of racism, Liddle said he was instead engaging in a debate about multiculturalism.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: In March 2010, the PCC upheld a complaint against Liddle, who became the first journalist to be censured over the contents of a blog, because he had not been able to prove his claim about the crime statistics.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: After the publication of London crime figures in June 2010, The Sunday Telegraph suggested Liddle was largely right on some of his claims, but that he was probably wrong on his claims about knife crimes and violent sex crimes.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: On 23 May 2013, Liddle wrote about the murder of soldier Lee Rigby near the Royal Artillery Barracks in Woolwich, London.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: In the original version of a blog article for The Spectator, he referred to the perpetrators as "two black savages".

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: After many objections to his language use, this phrase was modified.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: Liddle apologised.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: In a blog article for The Spectator website published shortly after the death of Nelson Mandela, Liddle wrote that the BBC coverage of his death was excessive, characterising it as "famous nice black man dies" and believing that Mandela had to "bear [the BBC's] entire self-flagellating white post-colonial bien pensant guilt."

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: Richard Garside, director of the Centre for Crime and Justice Studies, described him as an "attention seeking wind-up merchant".

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: In October 2019, Liddle penned a column in The Spectator commenting on the forthcoming December general election, which suggested that the election should be held on a Muslim holy day to reduce the Labour vote.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: The column was criticised by senior political figures including Chancellor of the Exchequer Sajid Javid and former Conservative Deputy Prime Minister David Lidington.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: Liddle defended the content as being humorous.

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: The article also criticised the Labour MP Rosie Duffield's recent speech about her experience of trying to exit an abusive relationship; Duffield described the article as "racist and misogynistic".

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: Giving a speech at Durham University in December 2021, Liddle said: "It is fairly easily proven that colonialism is not remotely the major cause of Africa's problems, just as it is very easy to prove that the educational underachievement of British people of Caribbean descent or African Americans is nothing to do with institutional or structural racism."

sentences.section: Comments on race, religion and colonialism
sentences.text: Many attendees walked out, with the speech later being described as "transphobic and racist" by the student newspaper.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: The Guardian reported on 8 January 2010 that the expected purchase of The Independent by Alexander Lebedev, a Russian billionaire, would be followed by the appointment of Liddle as editor.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Roy Greenslade wrote on 11 January that the reports were provoking a "major internal and external revolt" by The Independent'''s staff and readers.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In January 2010, the press drew attention to allegedly racist and misogynist comments posted under the username "monkeymfc"a name Liddle has usedon Millwall Online, a fan club web forum with no official connection to Millwall Football Club.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle attributed some of the comments to opposition fans logging in under his name to embarrass him.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: He later said he had written some of the posts that were being criticised.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: One post, in which he joked about not being able to smoke at Auschwitz, led to his being asked to explain what he meant in The Jewish Chronicle.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: While he said in June 2014 that his comments were taken out of context, he said that he did not regret making them.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: "No. Never.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Absolutely not.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: I thought about my mates at Millwall Online, God I respect them so much more than these other people, these ghastly fucking people."

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: The stories about Liddle's posts on Millwall Online apparently further reduced the likelihood of his being offered the job.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Finally, on 19 February, Stephen Brook of The Guardian reported that Liddle was no longer in the running for the post.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Tim Luckhurst, professor of journalism at the University of Kent, argued that Liddle's prospects of editing The Independent were nullified "by the people behind a viciously intolerant campaign of liberal bigotry".

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In November 2011, an article by Liddle for The Spectator suggested the trial of two men accused (and later convicted) of murdering Stephen Lawrence would not be fair.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: It was referred to the Attorney General Dominic Grieve by the judge for possible contempt of court, and he ordered the jurors not to read it.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Having decided that it might have breached a court order, Grieve passed the case to the Director of Public Prosecutions.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: The decision that The Spectator was to be prosecuted for breaching reporting restrictions was announced on 9 May 2012, with a court hearing scheduled for 7 June, although Liddle as the author was not himself liable for prosecution.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Fraser Nelson, the magazine's editor, announced that the prosecution would not be contested, and the magazine pleaded guilty at the hearing.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: The fine was £3,000, plus £2,000 compensation to Stephen Lawrence's parents and £625 costs.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In January 2012, Liddle wrote that many people in the UK were "pretending to be disabled" in his column for The Sun, an opinion defended by James Delingpole.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Frances Ryan in The Guardian criticised his comments.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In May 2015, the Independent Press Standards Organisation (IPSO) upheld a complaint from Trans Media Watch that Liddle had been discriminatory towards Emily Brothers, a blind and transgender Labour candidate at the 2015 general election, in two Sun columns published in December 2014 and January 2015.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In commenting in the way he had Liddle had breached two sections of the editors' code.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Writing in 2012 in The Spectator, Liddle stated that "the one thing stopping me from being a teacher was that I could not remotely conceive of not trying to shag the kids" and that he did not expect to "[dabble] much below year ten" (corresponding to age 14–15).

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In December 2020, Ash Sarkar tweeted about Liddle's article.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle was opposed to laws against viewing child sexual abuse material, writing in The Guardian in 2003 that "we should not be in the business of putting people in prison for simply looking at things".

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Jenni Murray said she was "shocked" at Liddle's "glib dismissal" of "any causal link between viewing child porn and abusing children".

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: During a parliamentary debate on the Psychoactive Substances Bill – which "makes it an offence to produce, supply, offer to supply, possess with intent to supply, possess on custodial premises, import or export psychoactive substances" the Conservative MP Crispin Blunt admitted he used amyl nitrite (poppers):

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: And would be directly affected by this legislation.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: And I was astonished to find that it's proposed they be banned and, frankly, so were very many gay men.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle responded in his Spectator blog: So, Crispin Blunt MP feels hurt because laws proscribing (or 'poppers') would criminalise the entire gay community.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: I would have thought that the requirement for amyl nitrate to relax the sphincter muscle and lube to accommodate entry was God's way of telling you that what you're about to do is unnatural and perverse.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Or your body's way of telling you – your call.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: So eeeeuw.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Crispin and others can always use a jemmy [crowbar] instead.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: The satirical magazine Private Eye described this as hypocritical, pointing out Liddle's account in The Sunday Times of using Viagra in July 2004.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: A spokesperson from the LGBT rights charity Stonewall called Liddle a "repeat offending bigot".

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In 2003, Liddle published a collection of short stories, Too Beautiful For You.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: He said he had always wanted to be a writer, and saw journalism as a cop-out.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: He was also the author of Love Will Destroy Everything (2007) and The Best of Liddle Britain (2007).

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Selfish, Whining Monkeys: How we Ended Up Greedy, Narcissistic and Unhappy appeared in 2014.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Admitting to having paid little attention to Liddle's journalism, Will Self, in his review for The Guardian wrote: "it's so much more authoritative to hear a man condemned out of his own mouth over 200-plus pages than it is to assay him on the basis of newspaper columns, which, by and large, favour polarised views tendentiously expressed."

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Despite his serious reservations about Liddle's writing, Self concludes: "The peculiar thing is that I can't find it in my heart of hearts to dislike the man, I think there's good in him and that he can change his bilious complexion."

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle responded to Self's review in an interview with Archie Bland of The Independent a few weeks later: "He reviewed what he thought I was, not what the book was about.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Bizarre.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: I think it's slightly deranged."

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In 2019, Liddle published The Great Betrayal, a book about Brexit.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: The book was reviewed positively by Matt Goodwin in The Sunday Times, who called it "a no-holds-barred attack on the Establishment's blocking of Brexit".

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Harry Mount at The Spectator called the book "very engaging", despite noting concerns that the book's claim of a betrayal of Brexit possibly proving to be unfounded.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: However, Fintan O'Toole writing for The Guardian said the book was "as untroubled by facts as by logic".

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In 2003, Liddle co-presented the short-lived BBC Two political show Weekend with Kate Silverton, described by The Independent on Sunday as "the worst programme anywhere, ever, in the history of time", and BBC Four's The Talk Show.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: He also became a team captain on Call My Bluff.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In The New Fundamentalists, a programme in the Dispatches strand broadcast in March 2006, Liddle, a member of the Church of England, condemned the rise of evangelicalism and Christian fundamentalism in Britain, especially the anti-Darwinian influence of such beliefs in faith schools, and criticised the social teaching and cultural influence of this strand of Christianity.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: The documentary was criticised by David Hilborn of the Evangelical Alliance, and by Rupert Kaye of the Association of Christian Teachers.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In The Trouble with Atheism, Liddle argued that atheists can be as dogmatic and intolerant as the adherents of religion.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle said, "History has shown us that it's not religion that's the problem, but any system of thought that insists that one group of people are inviolably in the right, whereas the others are in the wrong and must somehow be punished."

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle's Immigration Is a Time Bomb was broadcast by Channel 4 in 2005.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Complaints that followed it included that he should not have allowed British National Party leader Nick Griffin to speak unchallenged.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Ofcom adjudicated that the programme was fair, and the complaints were dismissed.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle subsequently argued, after Griffin was acquitted in February 2006 of two charges of inciting racial hatred, that the charges were "too ephemeral, too dependent upon the mindset and political disposition of the juror, and upon what is happening outside of the courtroom, on the streets."

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In April 2007, Liddle presented a two-hour-long theological documentary called The Bible Revolution, where he looked back in history to William Tyndale's translation of the Bible into English and the effect this had upon the English language.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: On 21 May 2007, he presented an hour-long documentary, Battle for the Holy Land: Love Thy Neighbour, about the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: He visited Bethlehem, Hebron, and the Israeli settlement of Tekoa.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle sought to examine whether Israel was a true liberal democracy in light of its treatment of the Palestinians.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: He also appeared in Channel 4's alternative election night episode of Come Dine with Me, along with Edwina Currie, Derek Hatton, and Brian Paddick.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle appeared on the BBC's Newsnight, hosted by Emily Maitlis, to discuss Brexit on 15 July 2019.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In the episode, Maitlis said Liddle wrote columns containing "consistent casual racism week after week" and asked him if he would describe himself as a racist.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: After the episode was broadcast, a complainant alleged that Maitlis was "sneering and bullying" towards Liddle.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: An investigation by the BBC upheld these complaints, saying that Maitlis was "persistent and personal" in her criticism of Liddle, thus "leaving her open to the charge that she had failed to be even-handed" in the discussion.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Aged 16, Liddle was a member of the Socialist Workers Party, remaining a member for about a year, and supported the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament (CND) around the same time.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: He campaigned for the Labour Party in the 1983 general election, canvassing votes door to door in full punk get-up.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: He estimated that, in doing so, "I must have singlehandedly lost my party a good 5,000 votes".

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: From 1983 to 1987, he worked as a speechwriter and researcher for Labour.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle supported Brexit.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: He joined the Social Democratic Party in 2019, saying that as a political movement "it stresses the commonality shared between citizens, rather than the differences."

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: He stood as a candidate for the SDP in Middlesbrough South and East Cleveland during the 2024 general election, a seat then held by the Conservative Simon Clarke.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle gained 1,835 votes and came fourth, with Labour defeating Clarke to win the seat.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle met Rachel Royce, a television presenter, at the BBC in 1993, and the couple soon became romantically involved.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: In January 2004 the couple married at a ceremony in Malaysia.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: They had been living in Heytesbury, Wiltshire, and had two sons together.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Six months later, Liddle moved in with Alicia Monckton, a 22-year-old receptionist at The Spectator.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: It transpired that he had cut short his honeymoon with Royce so that he could be with Monckton.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Following their divorce, Liddle and Royce exchanged attacks in the media.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle called her a "total slut and slattern", and Royce wrote an article in the Daily Mail titled "My cheating husband Rod, 10 bags of manure and me the bunny boiler.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: As for The Slapper[...] she's welcome to him."

sentences.text: On 5 May 2005, Liddle was arrested for common assault against Monckton, who was 20 weeks pregnant at the time.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: He admitted the offence and accepted a police caution, but said later that he did so only because it was the quickest way for him to be released and that he had not assaulted her.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Liddle died at James Cook University Hospital in Middlesbrough, on 2 August 2026, aged 66.

sentences.section: Independent editor rumour and Millwall supporters' website
sentences.text: Writing for The Daily Telegraph, Allison Pearson described Liddle as "a great British freedom fighter" and a "valiant warrior in the culture wars", as well as "a people's champion who united anyone and everyone with a brain and a heart".
